entry_points.text: Uninterruptible waits assert sleepable context, fast-path when true, then sleep via normal, I/O or caller-command scheduling.
Interruptible, killable, freezable and idle waits share fast-path plus core loop with distinct states and signal-aware return.
Timeout waits return remaining time and treat late satisfaction as success, including monotonic high-resolution forms.
Locked waits run a caller function with external lock held; generic forms drop a spinlock or mutex across uninterruptible sleep.
Bit waits fast-path on clear bit or successful atomic set before delegating. Boot wires default group; thread teardown is empty.

exports.text: Task lifetime uses a usage count with unconditional get, conditional get when non-zero, single release, bulk release and scope-exit cleanup.
Stack pinning returns the stack only on successful reference. Defaults report full capacity, zero pressure and task node from CPU.
Wake helpers support normal, interruptible, counted, locked and poll-keyed wakes plus protected variable wakes and bit-clear wakes.
I/O accounting counts bytes and syscalls when enabled. Virtual-time enablement and IRQ enter-exit charging follow generic tracking state.
Bit waits sleep until a bit clears; variable waits sleep on an address-derived queue until a condition holds, with timeout and lock forms.
Queue-head waits check a condition under a caller spinlock with interrupts disabled and sleep only when unsatisfied, with timeout variants.

hazards.text: During construction shared scan storage holds allocation flags, so early readers may see a small flag value until first refresh.
Poll-free wake may skip locking when idle and race last-entry removal, needing RCU hold by remover; core waits need double test.
Bit and variable waits may sleep; interruptible forms report signals and timeout forms return remaining time with zero meaning expiry.
Autogroup allocation failure warns and returns the default group, so callers must handle aliasing; sequence uses an atomic counter.
User, guest and IRQ accounting are inert in routed configs; pressure update, energy rebuild and frequency reference have no effect.
List, refcount, barrier, bit-test and spinlock helpers are owned by other dossiers and cited by sid only in this pass.

invariants.text: Stack end corruption uses a magic word. Containment checks tag-normalized addresses in one stack extent; spare-space query reports zero.
Heads start unlocked with empty lists. Insertion respects leading priority entries; activity checks emptiness with barrier-paired visibility.
Domain flags enumerate positions then bit masks. Span mask lives in trailing allocation; attributes default relaxation to disabled.
Entries bind to current task with default or caller callback and cleared flags. Bit keys record only word pointer and bit index.
Autogroup defaults to enabled with a 0-1 control. Init wires the initial task to a default group with refcount and semaphore.
Switch tracing requires current task with preempted tasks reported running. Skip reasons enumerate seven unsuitable or completed causes.
Guest accounting brackets kernel charging by setting then clearing a virtual-CPU flag on the current task.

locks.text: Raw spin unlock helpers use plain, interrupt-enabling or flag-restoring release and optionally drain then reinitialize a wake queue.
Queue spinlock serializes lists and most wakes; locked wakes require it held. Lock-IRQ waits drop and reacquire caller lock around sleep.
Simple wait heads serialize membership with an embedded raw spinlock; occupancy follows list emptiness with barrier-paired check.
Group sampling holds signal lock; group release holds global lock with IRQs saved. Protected wakes require a caller-held guard.

state_machines.text: Simple exclusive waits prepare, test, handle signals, sleep in a selected state and finalize; timeout forms carry remaining time.
Core waits loop prepare, test, signal abort, sleep and retest before finish; helpers preserve timeout and detect interruptible states.
Variable waits prepare on an address queue, test, check interruption and sleep, always removing the element before reporting.
Autogroups use refcounted create with online bring-up and detached destroy; scheduling groups unlink with deferred reclaim.

structs.text: Domains link parent, child, groups, timing, flags, stats, name and shared state. Topology levels bind mask and flags callbacks with per-CPU data.
Wait entries hold flags, private data, callback and list node; heads hold lock and list. Bit waits pair a key with a generic entry.
Deferred wake heads store first node and tail link; empty state uses a sentinel with tail pointing at the first slot.
Simple wait heads combine raw spinlock with task list; entries pair task pointer with linkage plus static initializers.
CPU accounting groups user, system and total time. User state, clone arguments and scheduling attributes use fixed ordered fields.
Clone ABI uses low byte for exit signal, low-word bits for sharing, high bits for extended controls, with 64 and 88 byte sizes.
Policies number normal, fifo, deadline and extensible classes with low-bit attribute flags, small wait flags and deadline-trace kinds.
Stacks derive from stored pointer or thread info with direction-dependent end computation and no-op or copying setup by configuration.
